title: Slice-anchored phased-promote controller with shadow-gate and resumable rollback
author: Asha Patel
release_notes: Adds a new slice-anchored phased promote controller that coordinates shadow fidelity gating and resumable rollback snapshots. Enables finer-grained canaries per customer slice, improves rollback reliability, and provides instrumentation for SLO-driven holdpoints.
description: Motivation: Our existing rollout controllers operate at coarse route-level granularity which makes phased promotes brittle for heterogenous customer populations. This PR introduces a SliceAnchoredPhasedPromote controller that attaches promote progress to logically-defined traffic slices and uses a shadow-fidelity gate plus resumable rollback snapshots to reduce blast radius and improve recoverability. High level: 1) Traffic slices are first validated via shadow playback and fidelity checks (latency/quality parity). 2) The controller increments live traffic to a slice in phases while monitoring slice-level metrics and SLO gates. 3) If fidelity gates fail, a resumable rollback snapshot is applied for that slice only (no global swap). 4) Controller maintains a small escrow of lightweight snapshots to allow time-boxed retries and a graded rewind. This is intended for Dedicated and Private customers where per-slice rollout semantics and auditability are required. What changed (summary): - New controller: controllers/slice_phased_promote.go (core reconcile loop, phase state machine, slice leasing and escrow manager). - Shadow fidelity gate: controllers/gates/shadow_fidelity.go (stateless comparator, configurable thresholds). - Snapshot/rollback plumbing: pkg/snapshot/escrow.go and integration with the routing plane to apply per-slice rewinds. - API surface: api/v1alpha1/slicepromote types and CRD conversion. - Console: console/rollouts/slice_view.tsx shows per-slice progress and one-click abort/rewind. - E2E tests: test/e2e/slice_promote_smoke_test.go and smoke fixtures. - Integration tests: ci/presubmit/slice_promote_integration.yml. Backwards compatibility: The new controller registers under a new CRD (SlicePromote) and does not alter existing Promote/Canary CRDs. Default behavior for customers who do not create SlicePromote objects is unchanged. Configuration: New feature flags: rollout.slice_promote.enabled (false by default), rollout.slice_promote.max_phase_duration, rollout.slice_promote.escrow_size. Rollout plan: Start behind feature flag in staging for 48 hours with synthetic slices, then enable for opt-in customers in Dedicated, observe SLOs for two weeks before general availability. Testing performed: Unit tests for reconcile transitions and escrow invariants, integration tests with simulated shadow playback, and a staging canary with three customer slices. CI: presubmit matrix runs unit, linters, and an integration job that exercises shadow playback (all green after one rerun due to ephemeral infra flakiness). Checklist: - [x] Controller implementation - [x] CRD and API validation - [x] Unit tests - [x] Integration/presubmit job - [x] Console view - [x] Docs draft added to redwood-docs (link: https://github.com/redwood/redwood-docs/pull/1892) - [x] Linear tickets linked Risks and mitigations: - Risk: Overlapping slice definitions could cause double-promotes. Mitigation: Lease-based slice ownership enforced by the controller; validation rejects overlapping slices. - Risk: Snapshot escrow growth under noisy traffic. Mitigation: escrow_size config and TTL eviction. Related work: builds on ENG-7120 (shadow playback harness) and ENG-7301 (per-route telemetry extrusion).

notes: This PR intentionally introduces feature-flag gating and a small default escrow to reduce blast radius at rollout time. The next work item (ENG-7483) expands observability hooks for slice-level distributed traces and adds a promote dry-run mode to simulate phased traffic without applying live changes.
